meaning.en: Withered trees and rotten stumps; figuratively, worthless things or people past their usefulness.
meaning.zh: 枯死的树木和腐烂的树桩，比喻衰老无用的人或物。

examples.zh: 园子里满是枯木朽株，需要彻底清理。
examples.en: The garden is full of dead wood and needs a thorough clearing.

examples.zh: 别把老同事看成枯木朽株，他们的经验最宝贵。
examples.en: Don't treat old colleagues as dead wood; their experience is the most valuable.

usage.en: Can be literal or used disparagingly of the old or obsolete; take care when applied to people.
usage.zh: 可指实物，也可贬称衰老或过时的人事，用于人时需谨慎。

meaning.en: To shift one's own trouble or blame onto someone else.
meaning.zh: 把自己的灾祸转嫁给别人。

examples.zh: 他想把责任推给别人，移祸江东。
examples.en: He tried to pin the responsibility on someone else, shifting the trouble onto another.

examples.zh: 公司出了事，经理试图移祸江东，让下属背锅。
examples.en: When the company hit trouble the manager tried to pass it on and make his staff carry the blame.

usage.en: Literary and critical; Jiangdong stands for the Wu territory in the Three Kingdoms story, now generally for 'another party'.
usage.zh: 书面语，含贬义；“江东”原指三国时的东吴，今泛指他方。

meaning.en: To confess fully and hold nothing back (of a suspect).
meaning.zh: 毫不隐瞒地承认罪行。

examples.zh: 嫌疑人对犯罪事实供认不讳。
examples.en: The suspect confessed to the crime in full.

examples.zh: 面对证据，他只好供认不讳。
examples.en: Faced with the evidence he had no choice but to confess everything.

usage.en: Legal and news register; used of wrongdoing, not good deeds.
usage.zh: 多用于法律、新闻，指承认罪行。

natural: when you know your fault, correct it

meaning.en: To correct a mistake as soon as one realises it.
meaning.zh: 知道自己有过错，一定要改正。

examples.zh: 知过必改，善莫大焉。
examples.en: To mend one's error on seeing it is a great virtue.

examples.zh: 他是个知过必改的人，批评过一次就不再犯。
examples.en: He corrects himself once he sees a fault and doesn't repeat it after a single criticism.

story.en: The Thousand Character Classic advises: 'Know your faults and be sure to correct them; keep what you are able to do and never forget it' (知过必改，得能莫忘).

usage.en: Positive; often paired with 得能莫忘 in the Thousand Character Classic, or used as a motto.
usage.zh: 褒义，《千字文》中与“得能莫忘”相连，也常作格言。

pinyin: xì jié jué dìng chéng bài

meaning.en: Small details determine whether a project succeeds or fails.
meaning.zh: 小处是否做好，决定整件事情的成败。

equivalents: the devil is in the details

examples.zh: 细节决定成败，这次失败就败在一个小数点上。
examples.en: Details decide success or failure, and this failure came down to a decimal point.

examples.zh: 设计师常说细节决定成败。
examples.en: Designers often say details make or break a work.

usage.en: A modern business and management slogan, now common in workplaces and school essays.
usage.zh: 现代常用的管理、职场口号，也见于作文。

pinyin: zhī shi jiù shì lì liàng

meaning.en: Knowledge gives people the strength to change themselves and the world.
meaning.zh: 掌握知识就拥有了改变世界的力量。

examples.zh: 老师在黑板上写下“知识就是力量”。
examples.en: The teacher wrote 'Knowledge is power' on the blackboard.

examples.zh: 知识就是力量，所以我们要坚持读书。
examples.en: Knowledge is power, so we must keep reading.

story.en: Francis Bacon wrote in Latin 'ipsa scientia potestas est' (knowledge itself is power) in his Meditationes Sacrae.
story.zh: 培根在《神圣沉思录》中写下拉丁文“ipsa scientia potestas est”（知识本身就是力量）。

usage.en: A translated saying attributed to Francis Bacon, widely used in schools and public slogans.
usage.zh: 译自培根的名言，在学校和公共宣传中广泛使用。

meaning.en: To lure someone into a trap.
meaning.zh: 设下圈套，诱使对方陷入其中。

examples.zh: 对方故意示弱，是想引君入瓮。
examples.en: The other side feigned weakness on purpose to lure us into a trap.

examples.zh: 警方放出假消息，引君入瓮，抓获了嫌疑人。
examples.en: The police leaked false news to lure the suspect in and arrested him.

usage.en: Related to 请君入瓮 (to use someone's own method against them) but simply stresses luring into a trap.
usage.zh: 与“请君入瓮”相近，但只强调设圈套诱人上当，不含“以其人之道还治其人之身”之意。

natural: catch a white wolf with empty hands

meaning.en: To get something valuable for nothing, usually by clever manoeuvring or tricks.
meaning.zh: 不付出本钱，靠手段谋取利益。

equivalents: make money out of thin air

examples.zh: 他想空手套白狼，用别人的钱办自己的公司。
examples.en: He wanted to start up on other people's money without risking anything.

examples.zh: 空手套白狼的生意长久不了。
examples.en: A business that gets something for nothing can't last.

usage.en: Colloquial; sometimes grudging admiration of cleverness, mostly disapproving of risky or shady schemes.
usage.zh: 口语，多含贬义，有时也带些佩服。

natural: the view of a frog in a well

meaning.en: A narrow outlook, like that of a frog that has never seen beyond its well.
meaning.zh: 见识狭隘，像井里的青蛙只看见一小块天。

examples.zh: 不出国门，就容易陷入井蛙之见。
examples.en: If you never leave your country you can easily fall into a narrow view.

examples.zh: 我这是井蛙之见，让您见笑了。
examples.en: This is only my narrow view; forgive me.

story.en: Zhuangzi: 'You cannot talk of the sea to a frog in a well, for it is confined to its space' (井蛙不可以语于海者，拘于虚也).
story.zh: 《庄子·秋水》：“井蛙不可以语于海者，拘于虚也。”

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: Can be self-deprecating (我这只是井蛙之见) or critical of others.
usage.zh: 可自谦（“这只是井蛙之见”），也可批评他人。

pinyin: rén jiē kě yǐ wéi yáo shùn
literal: everyone · all · can · become · Yao · Shun
natural: everyone can become a Yao or a Shun

meaning.en: Anyone can become a sage through self-cultivation.
meaning.zh: 每个人通过修养都可以成为尧舜那样的圣人。

equivalents: every man can be a saint

examples.zh: 孟子讲“人皆可以为尧舜”，强调教育的力量。
examples.en: Mencius said that everyone can be a Yao or Shun, stressing the power of education.

examples.zh: 人皆可以为尧舜，关键在于是否肯修身。
examples.en: Anyone can become a sage; it depends on whether one cultivates oneself.

story.en: When asked whether it was true that anyone could be a Yao or Shun, Mencius answered 'Yes' (人皆可以为尧舜).
story.zh: 曹交问：“人皆可以为尧舜，有诸？”孟子答：“然。”

usage.en: Quoted when speaking of moral self-improvement or the equality of human potential.
usage.zh: 谈到修身或人性平等的潜力时常引用。

natural: divine troops come down from the sky

meaning.en: Troops or helpers who appear suddenly and unexpectedly, as if sent from heaven.
meaning.zh: 军队或援助突然出现，像是从天上降下来。

examples.zh: 正当大家束手无策时，救援队神兵天降。
examples.en: Just when everyone was at a loss, the rescue team appeared as if from nowhere.

examples.zh: 特种部队神兵天降，敌人措手不及。
examples.en: The special forces dropped in unexpectedly and caught the enemy off guard.

usage.en: Usually praise for a timely, unexpected arrival; also used humorously.
usage.zh: 多赞扬及时而意外的到来，也可诙谐使用。

pinyin: néng zhě shàng yōng zhě xià
literal: able · ones · rise · mediocre · ones · step down
natural: the able go up, the mediocre go down

meaning.en: Capable people should be promoted and the mediocre removed from posts.
meaning.zh: 有能力的人应当得到任用，平庸的人则应让位。

equivalents: promote the able, remove the mediocre

examples.zh: 用人要能者上庸者下，不能论资排辈。
examples.en: In appointments the able should rise and the mediocre step aside, not go by seniority.

examples.zh: 公司实行能者上庸者下的制度。
examples.en: The company applies a system where the able rise and the mediocre make way.

usage.en: Often appears in management and personnel contexts; usually written 能者上，庸者下 (and often with 平者让).
usage.zh: 多见于人事管理，也写作“能者上，庸者下”，常与“平者让”连用。

meaning.en: A policy of letting wealth remain with the people rather than the state.
meaning.zh: 让财富留在百姓手中，而不是集中于国家或官府。

equivalents: let wealth stay with the people

examples.zh: 长久之计在于藏富于民。
examples.en: The long-term plan lies in leaving the wealth with the people.

examples.zh: 政府应该减税，藏富于民。
examples.en: The government should cut taxes and let wealth stay with the people.

usage.en: Economic and political writing; often argues for low taxes or people's livelihood.
usage.zh: 多用于经济、政治论述，常主张减税、改善民生。

meaning.en: An extravagant banquet of rare delicacies.
meaning.zh: 形容菜肴极其珍贵丰盛。

examples.zh: 宫廷宴会烹龙炮凤，极尽奢华。
examples.en: The palace banquets were a feast of rare delicacies and utterly lavish.

examples.zh: 别说烹龙炮凤，粗茶淡饭他也吃得香。
examples.en: Never mind rare delicacies; he enjoys even plain tea and rice.

usage.en: Literary hyperbole; no actual dragons or phoenixes involved.
usage.zh: 书面夸张，并非真有龙凤。

story.en: Li He's 'Bring in the Wine' has the line 'boiled dragon and roasted phoenix, the jade fat weeps', picturing a lavish feast of rare delicacies.
story.zh: 李贺《将进酒》有“烹龙炮凤玉脂泣，罗帏绣幕围香风”，写珍馐美味的奢华盛宴。

natural: the sun is three zhang high

meaning.en: The sun is already high in the sky; it is late in the morning.
meaning.zh: 太阳已经升得很高，形容时间不早。

examples.zh: 他睡到日高三丈才起床。
examples.en: He slept until the sun was high.

examples.zh: 日高三丈，院子里一个人也没有。
examples.en: The sun was high and there was no one in the courtyard.

usage.en: Often hints at oversleeping. The more common synonym is 日上三竿.
usage.zh: 常暗示睡懒觉，较常用的同义说法是“日上三竿”。

natural: use friends to support one's virtue

meaning.en: To rely on friends to help one grow in virtue.
meaning.zh: 借助朋友的帮助，培养自己的仁德。

equivalents: friends help one grow in virtue

examples.zh: 君子以文会友，以友辅仁。
examples.en: The gentleman gathers friends through letters and uses friends to support his virtue.

examples.zh: 读书会让我们以友辅仁，共同进步。
examples.en: The book club lets us improve together through friendship.

story.en: Zengzi said: 'The gentleman gathers friends through learning and uses friends to support humaneness' (君子以文会友，以友辅仁).
story.zh: 曾子曰：“君子以文会友，以友辅仁。”

usage.en: Usually quoted in full with 以文会友; used of friendships that improve us.
usage.zh: 常与“以文会友”连用，指能促人向上的友谊。

meaning.en: A deal is done, with payment and goods fully exchanged and no further claims.
meaning.zh: 钱已付清，货已交完，买卖两清。

examples.zh: 合同写明银货两讫，双方不再有任何债务。
examples.en: The contract states payment and delivery are complete and neither side owes anything more.

examples.zh: 买卖一旦银货两讫，就概不退换。
examples.en: Once a sale is settled, no returns or exchanges.

usage.en: Commonly seen on receipts, contracts and shop signs; formal but often slightly dated.
usage.zh: 常见于收据、合同、店铺告示，书面语，略显旧式。

meaning.en: A minor official of little importance; sometimes a self-mocking description of a low post.
meaning.zh: 指官职很小的官，常用于自嘲或讥讽。

examples.zh: 他只是个芝麻小官，哪有权力批这笔钱。
examples.en: He's only a minor official; he has no power to approve this money.

examples.zh: 别看他是芝麻小官，架子倒不小。
examples.en: He may be a petty official, but he puts on quite some airs.

usage.en: Casual, often self-mocking or sarcastic; also 芝麻官.
usage.zh: 口语，常自嘲或讽刺；也说“芝麻官”。

literal: pull out · hairs · hard · to count
natural: even pulling out one's hair would not count them

meaning.en: So many crimes that they cannot be counted, even by plucking out one's hair one hair per crime.
meaning.zh: 罪行多得数不清，即使拔下头发来数也数不完。

examples.zh: 贪官的罪行擢发难数。
examples.en: The corrupt official's crimes are too many to count.

examples.zh: 他欠下的恶债擢发难数，没人愿意再借钱给他。
examples.en: The bad debts he owes are beyond counting; nobody will lend him more.

story.en: Fan Sui asked Xu Jia how many crimes he had; Xu Jia answered that plucking out all his hairs to count them would still not be enough (擢贾之发以续贾之罪，尚未足).
story.zh: 范雎问须贾有多少罪过，须贾答：“擢贾之发以续贾之罪，尚未足。”

usage.en: Literary and condemning; always about wrongdoing.
usage.zh: 书面语，用于谴责，只指罪过。

meaning.en: Slaughter so terrible that blood floods the battlefield and floats the pestles.
meaning.zh: 形容战斗惨烈，死伤极多，血流成河。

examples.zh: 那场战役血流漂杵，惨不忍睹。
examples.en: That battle was a bloodbath, too horrible to look at.

examples.zh: 史书里有关于血流漂杵的描写。
examples.en: The histories describe scenes where blood ran in rivers.

story.en: Mencius doubted the Book of Documents' account of the Zhou conquest: 'With the most humane attacking the most inhumane, how could the blood have floated the pestles?' (何其血之流杵也).
story.zh: 孟子质疑《尚书·武成》所载：“以至仁伐至不仁，而何其血之流杵也？”

usage.en: Literary; Mencius doubted the old record of 血流漂杵 at Mu Ye, saying a benevolent army would not produce such slaughter.
usage.zh: 书面语；孟子质疑《武成》中牧野之战血流漂杵的记载，认为仁义之师不会如此杀戮。

meaning.en: To stop loving one person and fall for someone else.
meaning.zh: 感情转移，爱上了别人。

examples.zh: 她发现男友移情别恋，选择了分手。
examples.en: She found out her boyfriend had fallen for someone else and broke up.

examples.zh: 剧中人物移情别恋，造成了悲剧。
examples.en: A character's change of heart leads to tragedy in the play.

usage.en: Mostly about romantic love; critical of the person who changes affection.
usage.zh: 多用于恋爱，含批评。

meaning.en: Contributions that deserve full recognition and cannot be ignored.
meaning.zh: 功劳很大，不能抹杀。

examples.zh: 这次成功，各位志愿者功不可没。
examples.en: All the volunteers deserve full credit for this success.

examples.zh: 他在公司创业初期功不可没。
examples.en: His role in the company's early days cannot be overlooked.

usage.en: Common in speeches and news when giving credit; predicate.
usage.zh: 常用于表彰、致谢，多作谓语。

natural: the years of eighty or ninety

meaning.en: Extreme old age, in one's eighties or nineties.
meaning.zh: 指八九十岁的高龄。

examples.zh: 爷爷已到耄耋之年，身体依然硬朗。
examples.en: Grandfather has reached his eighties or nineties and is still hale.

examples.zh: 这位耄耋之年的画家仍坚持每天作画。
examples.en: The artist, in his nineties, still paints every day.

usage.en: Respectful, formal term for very old people; used for others, never of oneself.
usage.zh: 对高龄者的尊称，多用于他人，不用于自称。
